4.73.m: Agastya said:
Having approached Trilocana, what did the god of gods, the six-faced one,
joined with the Mother of the Universe, do next? Tell that quickly.
Skanda said:
O pot-born sage, I shall tell you what has been asked; listen.
The sacred seat named Virajas, which is proclaimed to grant all perfections—
merely by the darśana of that seat, a man becomes free of dust;
where that great liṅga Trilocana is located in Vārāṇasī,
there is the sacred ford known as Pilipilā, renowned in the waters of the heavenly river;
that sacred ford in Kāśī is praised as containing all sacred fords.
Because whatever gods, seers, mortals, and serpents dwell within the three worlds,
together with rivers, mountains, and forests, are present there, O sage,

4.73.s: tadārabhya ca tattīrthaṃ tacca liṃgaṃ trilocanam ..
4.73.d: तदारभ्य च तत्तीर्थं तच्च लिंगं त्रिलोचनम् ..
4.73.m: from that time forth, that sacred ford and that liṅga Trilocana
became known as Triviṣṭapa, and for that reason it is supreme.
The greatness of the Triviṣṭapa liṅga, spoken by the bearer of the Pināka

4.73.s: jagajjananyāḥ purato yathā vacmi tathā mune ..7..

The Goddess said:
O god of gods, lord of the world, Śarva, all-giver, all-pervading one,
all-seeing, progenitor of all, I ask something; speak of it.
This dear sacred field of yours is the sovereign medicine for the seed of karma,

4.73.s: naiḥśreyasyāḥ śriyo gehaṃ mamāpi prītidaṃ mahat ..9..
4.73.d: नैःश्रेयस्याः श्रियो गेहं ममापि प्रीतिदं महत् ..9..

Before even a grain of dust of this sacred field, the three worlds are like a blade of grass;
by whom can the greatness of it all around be comprehended?
Whatever liṅgas exist here, all of them without doubt
are causes of liberation, and they are self-manifest as well.
Even if this is so, nonetheless, O Lord, you should declare the distinction:
Which liṅgas in Kāśī are beginningless and eternally perfected, O Śaṃkara,

Taking compassion upon me, O ocean of the nectar of mercy,
tell me this, O Śambhu! I bow at your feet."
Hearing this well-spoken speech of the goddess, the great Lord
spoke, O best of beings, of the great liṅgas to the enemy of Vindhya:
"By the mere hearing of whose names heaps of sins are destroyed,
and the store of merit that causes liberation in Kāśī is acquired."
The God of gods said:
"Listen, O goddess, to the supreme secret, the cause of liberation in this sacred field,
which even Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, and the other [gods] do not know at all.
Innumerable are the liṅgas in the Ānandakānana, O daughter of Parvata:
gross and subtle, made of various kinds of gems,
made of various minerals, O Lady, and many fashioned of stone;
many self-manifest ones, and, oh, those installed by gods and seers,
worshipped by Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Rakṣases,
and by Asuras, serpents, mortals, Dānavas, and hosts of apsarases;
marked with their respective names by the elephants of the quarters, mountains, sacred fords, bears, monkeys, Kinnaras,
and birds and other creatures, O goddess.
Those installed here are also causes of liberation—
both the invisible and the visible, even those in a dilapidated condition, my dear,

4.73.s: bhagnānyapi ca kālena tāni pūjyāni suṃdari..
4.73.d: भग्नान्यपि च कालेन तानि पूज्यानि सुंदरि..
4.73.m: and even those broken by time are worthy of worship, O beautiful woman.
Numbered once by me, they were hundreds of parārdhas.
Even in the water of the Gaṅgā there stand indeed six hundred million
perfected liṅgas, O Lady; in the Kali age they have become invisible.
Since that day of counting, O dear one, of those which have been installed

4.73.s: pratiṣṭhitāni yānīha teṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate ..27..
4.73.d: प्रतिष्ठितानि यानीह तेषां संख्या न विद्यते ..27..
4.73.m: here by my devotees, there is no count.

4.73.s: tvayā tu yāni pṛṣṭāni yairidaṃ kṣetramuttamam ..
4.73.d: त्वया तु यानि पृष्टानि यैरिदं क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् ..
4.73.m: Those, however, about which you asked, by which this supreme sacred field [was established],
those liṅgas that are the causes of liberation I shall proclaim, O beautiful woman.
In the Kali age they will become hidden, O daughter of the king of mountains;

4.73.s: paraṃ teṣāṃ prabhāvo yaḥ svasvasthānaṃ na hāsyati .. 29 ..
4.73.d: परं तेषां प्रभावो यः स्वस्वस्थानं न हास्यति .. 29 ..
4.73.m: yet their power shall not depart from their respective places.

4.73.s: kalikalmaṣapuṣṭā ye ye duṣṭā nāstikāḥ śaṭhāḥ ..

4.73.m: Those who are nurtured on the impurities of the Kali age, the wicked, the atheists, the deceitful,
will not even know the names of these perfected liṅgas here.
Even by hearing the names of these liṅgas here, O fair-faced woman,
sins are brought to destruction and heaps of merit increase.

4.73.s: oṃkāraḥ prathamaṃ liṃgaṃ dvitīyaṃ ca trilocanam ..
4.73.d: ओंकारः प्रथमं लिंगं द्वितीयं च त्रिलोचनम् ..
4.73.m: The first liṅga is Oṃkāra, and the second is Trilocana;
the third is Mahādeva, and the fourth is Kṛttivāsas;
Ratneśa is the fifth liṅga, and the sixth is named Candreśvara;
Kedāra is the seventh liṅga, and Dharmeśa is the eighth, my dear;

4.73.s: vīreśvaraṃ ca navamaṃ kāmeśaṃ daśamaṃ viduḥ ..
4.73.d: वीरेश्वरं च नवमं कामेशं दशमं विदुः ..
4.73.m: and the ninth is Vīreśvara; Kāmeśa is known as the tenth;
the auspicious liṅga Viśvakarmeśvara is the supreme eleventh;
the twelfth is Maṇikarṇīśa; the thirteenth is Avimukta;
and the fourteenth great liṅga is my [form] named Viśveśvara.
O dear, O beautiful woman, these fourteen are the causes of prosperity;
this assemblage of them here is declared to be the sacred field of liberation.
These are the supreme presiding deities of this sacred field;
when worshipped, they bestow upon men the glory of final beatitude.
In the Ānandakānana, these are declared for the sake of liberation, O beautiful one;
these fourteen great liṅgas, O dear one, are to be worshipped by embodied beings.
Beginning each month from the auspicious first day of the fortnight,
a pilgrimage to these principal liṅgas should be undertaken with effort.
Without worshipping Mahādeva in these liṅgas, O pot-born one,

4.73.s: kaḥ kāśyāṃ mokṣamāpnoti satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..4.2.73.40..
4.73.m: who attains liberation in Kāśī? This is the truth, the truth again and again.
Therefore, with every effort, by those desiring the fruit of Kāśī,
these liṅgas must be worshipped with supreme devotion, O sage."
Agastya said:
"Are these alone the great liṅgas, or are there others, O six-faced one,
that are causes of liberation here? If there are, then tell me."
Skanda said:
"There are also other great liṅgas here, O you of noble vows,
which will indeed remain hidden through the power of the Kali [age].
Only he who has perpetual devotion to Īśvara and knows best the true reality of Kāśī,

4.73.s: sa evaitāni liṃgāni vetsyatyanyo na kaścana .. 44 ..
4.73.d: स एवैतानि लिंगानि वेत्स्यत्यन्यो न कश्चन .. 44 ..
4.73.m: will know these liṅgas, and no one else.
[Liṅgas] by the mere utterance of whose names the impurities of the Kali [age] are destroyed:
Amṛteśa, Tārakeśa, Jñāneśa, Karuṇeśvara,
Mokṣadvāreśvara, and likewise Svargadvāreśvara,
Brahmeśa, Lāṅgala, and likewise Vṛddhakāleśvara,
Vṛṣeśa, Caṇḍīśa, Nandikeśa, and Maheśvara,
and the liṅga renowned here as the fourteenth, Jyotīrūpeśvara.
These are the fourteen great liṅgas in Kāśī, O beautiful woman;
these liṅgas in Ānandakānana are the causes of liberation.
They should never be declared to those whose intellects are corrupted by the Kali [age].
Whoever propitiates these fourteen liṅgas here,
for him there is never any return to the path of worldly existence.
This peerless treasury of Kāśī must not be revealed everywhere and anywhere.
Even the name of these liṅgas, O goddess, removes suffering even in great misfortune.
This is the supreme secret of this sacred field, O fair-faced woman.
All fourteen liṅgas indeed bring about my presence;
this alone is the heart of Avimukta, O daughter of the king of mountains!

4.73.s: imāni yāni liṃgāni sarveṣāṃ muktidāni hi ..
4.73.d: इमानि यानि लिंगानि सर्वेषां मुक्तिदानि हि ..
4.73.m: These liṅgas, which indeed grant liberation to all—
taking from everywhere the essence of each individual world,
I made them myself out of compassion for great devotion.

4.73.s: asminkṣetre dhruvaṃ muktiriti yā prathiti priye ..
4.73.d: अस्मिन्क्षेत्रे ध्रुवं मुक्तिरिति या प्रथिति प्रिये ..
4.73.m: The renown which holds that 'in this sacred field liberation is certain', O dear one—
the cause of that is these fourteen liṅgas of mine.

4.73.s: ta eva vratinaḥ kāṃte ta eva ca tapasvinaḥ..
4.73.d: त एव व्रतिनः कांते त एव च तपस्विनः..
4.73.m: They alone are keepers of vows, O beloved, they alone have performed austerities,
by whom, as devotees, these liṅgas in Ānandakānana have been meditated upon.
They alone have practiced true yoga, they alone have given gifts,
by whom these liṅgas in Kāśī have been seen, even from afar.
Whatever duties of sacrificial rites and public works have been prescribed by the best of sages,

4.73.s: te sarve tena vihitā yāvajjīvaṃ nirenasā .. 57 ..
4.73.d: ते सर्वे तेन विहिता यावज्जीवं निरेनसा .. 57 ..
4.73.m: all of them have been performed by that sinless person for life,
by whom, having reached Avimukta, O Pārvatī,
these great liṅgas have been worshipped even once here; he is liberated, there is no doubt about this."
Skanda said:

4.73.s: anyānyapi ca viṃdhyāre devyai proktāni śaṃbhunā ..
4.73.d: अन्यान्यपि च विंध्यारे देव्यै प्रोक्तानि शंभुना ..
4.73.m: "O enemy of the Vindhya, others too were told to the goddess by Śambhu,
for the sake of his devotees' welfare; hear them now, O elder brother:
Śaileśa, Saṅgameśa, Svarlīna, Madhyameśvara,
Hiraṇyagarbha, Īśāna, Goprekṣa, Vṛṣabhadhvaja,

4.73.s: upaśāṃta śivo jyeṣṭho nivāseśvara eva ca ..
4.73.d: उपशांत शिवो ज्येष्ठो निवासेश्वर एव च ..
4.73.m: Upaśāntaśiva, Jyeṣṭha, and Nivāseśvara,
Śukreśa, Vyāghraliṅga, and Jambukeśa as the fourteenth.
O sage, these are the fourteen great abodes;
even from serving them a man attains liberation.
Beginning diligently from the first lunar day of the dark fortnight of Caitra,
up to the fourteenth, these liṅgas should be worshipped by the virtuous.
An annual pilgrimage to them, accompanied by a great festival,
should be properly performed by seekers of liberation, granting the full attainment of the sacred field.
Having beheld with effort these fourteen great liṅgas, O sage,

4.73.s: dṛṣṭvā na jāyate jaṃtuḥ saṃsāre duḥkhasāgare ..65..
4.73.d: दृष्ट्वा न जायते जंतुः संसारे दुःखसागरे ..65..
4.73.m: a creature is not born again in worldly existence, the ocean of sorrow.
'This alone is the supreme reality of the sacred field, O dear one, for certain;
this very thing is the great medicine for those seized by the disease of worldly existence.
This is the Upaniṣad of the sacred field, this is the supreme seed of liberation;
this row of liṅgas, O dear one, is a forest fire to the forest of karma.
The greatness of each one of these liṅgas is without beginning or end;
it is fully known only by me, O goddess, and by no one else.'

4.73.s: iti śrutvā mune prāha devī hṛṣṭatanūruhā ..
4.73.d: इति श्रुत्वा मुने प्राह देवी हृष्टतनूरुहा ..
4.73.m: Having heard this, O sage, the goddess, with bristling hair,
bowed down to god Īśāna, the all-knowing, all-bestowing Śiva, and said:
The goddess said:
"Having heard this supreme secret in Kāśī which has been declared,
my mind has become exceedingly eager, O beloved!
Since it was said that each liṅga is the supreme, greater essence,
which is the cause of supreme nirvāṇa in Kāśī, O Lord of Causes!
Tell me, O Lord of the Universe, the majesty of each one of these,
of the fourteen liṅgas that destroy sin upon being heard.
How did the liṅga of Oṃkāreśa come to be here
from that most holy sacred field of Amarakaṇṭaka?
What is the nature of this Oṃkāra, and what is its majesty, O Hara?
By whom was it worshipped formerly, and what did it grant when worshipped?
Having brought this nectar-like speech of Mṛḍānī within the range of his hearing,
the God related the most wondrous story of Oṃkāra.
The God of gods said:
Listen to the story, O Aparṇā! I shall describe it before you,
how the manifestation of the liṅga of Oṃkāra took place here.
Formerly here in the Ānandavana, by Brahmā, the source of the universe,
tapas was performed, O great goddess, as he maintained supreme absorption.
Then, when a thousand yugas had elapsed, splitting open the seven Pātālas,
a light arose before him, illuminating the faces of the quarters.
That which had manifested within through sincere absorption—
that very supreme splendour manifested outside for the Creator.
From the cracking sound 'caṭa-caṭā' of the burst ground,
from that noise the self-controlled Creator gradually broke his absorption.
As the Creator, relinquishing that meditation, opened his eyes
and looked ahead, he then beheld before him the primordial syllable:
the syllable 'A', endowed with sattva, the field of the Ṛg[veda], the protector of creation,
the very self of Nārāyaṇa, established beyond darkness.
Then in front of that, the syllable 'U', whose form is rajas, the source of the Yajur[veda],
the creator of all, reflected as if it were his own form;
resembling an abode of continuous darkness, before that
he then beheld the syllable 'M', essentially consisting of tamas,
the source of the Sāma[veda], the cause of dissolution, having the visible form of Rudra.
Then in front of that, the meditator welcomed as a guest to his eyes
the form consisting of the universe, with qualities and also without qualities,
the abode of the unuttered sound, an embodiment of supreme bliss,
which is renowned as the sonic absolute, the cause of all that consists of speech.
Then above the sound, having the form of a point, higher than the highest,

4.73.s: kāraṇaṃ kāraṇānāṃ ca jagadyoniṃ ca taṃ param ..
4.73.d: कारणं कारणानां च जगद्योनिं च तं परम् ..
4.73.m: the cause of causes and the source of the world, that supreme reality,
the Creator beheld, brought within the range of his vision by tapas.
Renowned as 'Om' because of protecting everything by its power;
because it elevates the devotee, it is proclaimed as 'Om'.
Though formless, richly endowed with form, it was brought before the eyes by the Creator.
Because it ferries across the ocean of worldly existence one whose mind is intent on chanting it,

4.73.s: tatastāra iti khyāto yastaṃ brahmā vyalokayat .. 4.2.73.90 ..
4.73.d: ततस्तार इति ख्यातो यस्तं ब्रह्मा व्यलोकयत् .. 4.2.73.90 ..
4.73.m: it is therefore known as Tāra ('the deliverer'), which Brahmā beheld.
Because it is praised by all who desire supreme nirvāṇa,
and is superior to all, it is therefore celebrated by them as Praṇava.
Because it leads the man who serves it to the supreme state,
the Creator therefore beheld that peaceful Praṇava directly.
Composed of the threefold Vedas, the fourth, transcending the fourth, the self of all,
whose essence is sound and point—that was beheld by the one who rides the swan.

4.73.s: prāvartaṃta yato vedāḥ sāṃgāḥ sarvasya yonayaḥ ..
4.73.d: प्रावर्तंत यतो वेदाः सांगाः सर्वस्य योनयः ..
4.73.m: That from which the Vedas, with their limbs, the wombs of everything, originated—
that beginning of the Vedas was beheld before him by the lotus-born [Brahmā].
The bull who is bound in three ways and bellows loudly, consisting of great light—
that supreme reality was made an object of vision by Parameṣṭhin.
Four were his horns, and seven indeed his hands,

4.73.s: dve śīrṣe ca trayaḥ pādāḥ sa devo vidhinaikṣata .. 96 ..
4.73.d: द्वे शीर्षे च त्रयः पादाः स देवो विधिनैक्षत .. 96 ..
4.73.m: two heads and three feet: that deity was beheld by the Creator.
That in which all that has been, will be, and is presently existing is dissolved—
that seed devoid of seed was seen by Druhiṇa.
Wherein this vessel of the world up to Brahmā, dissolved, is sought,
and therefore is worshipped by the virtuous: that liṅga was beheld.

4.73.s: paṃcārthā yatra bhāsaṃte paṃcabrahmamayaṃ hi yat ..
4.73.d: पंचार्था यत्र भासंते पंचब्रह्ममयं हि यत् ..
4.73.m: Wherein the five categories shine forth, which indeed consists of the five brahmans,
which has the nature of the primal five: that indeed was beheld by Brahmā.
Having then beheld that Lord who has the form of a liṅga,
[Brahmā] praised Śaṃkara, who consists of the five syllables and is distinct from the manifested world: (100)
Brahmā said: / Homage to you whose form is the syllable Oṃ; homage to you who bear an imperishable body;
Homage to the origin of the letters beginning with ‘a’, O Sadāśiva! (1)
You are the letter ‘a’, you are the letter ‘u’, you are the letter ‘m’, O formless one!
Homage to you who have the form of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma, and who transcend all form! (2)
Homage to you whose self is the sonic resonance (nāda); homage to you whose self is the point (bindu) and digit (kalā);
To you whose form is both non-liṅga and liṅga, whose nature is all forms! (3)
Homage to you, the treasury of splendor, O you who are devoid of end and origin!

4.73.s: namo bhavāya rudrāya śarvāya ca namostute .. 4 ..
4.73.d: नमो भवाय रुद्राय शर्वाय च नमोस्तुते .. 4 ..
4.73.m: Homage to Bhava, to Rudra, and homage be to you, O Śarva! (4)

4.73.s: nama ugrāya bhīmāya paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ ..
4.73.d: नम उग्राय भीमाय पशूनां पतये नमः ..
4.73.m: Homage to the fierce one, to the terrible one; homage to the lord of beasts (Paśupati)!
Homage to the one whose form is the praṇava; homage be to you, the source of existence! (5)
Homage to you who are free from illusion; homage to you who are exceedingly auspicious;
Homage to you who wear matted hair; homage be to you, O blue-throated one! (6)
Homage to you, the most bountiful, O dweller on the mountain, enveloped in rays of light;
Homage to the one who is not short, to the dwarf, to the vast, to the one in the form of an elder! (7)
Homage to you, the teacher of Kumāra; homage to the one whose body is like a youth;
Homage to the white, to the black, to the yellow, to the dawn-hued form! (8)
Homage to the smoke-colored, to the reddish-brown; homage to the one of variegated luster;
Homage to the pale-red colored; homage to the green-rayed! (9)
Homage to the one whose form is diverse colors, to the lord of phonemes and colors;
Homage to you whose form is vowels; homage to the one whose form is consonants! (110)
Homage, homage to the high-pitched, to the unaccented, to the circumflex accent;
Homage to you, the lord of short, long, and prolated vowels, accompanied by the visarga! (11)
Homage to you whose form is the anusvāra, O nasalized one;
Homage to the non-nasalized, to the one who takes the form of dental and palatal sounds! (12)
Homage to the one whose form is labial and pectoral sounds; homage to the one whose form is the sibilants and aspirate;
Homage to you who are the semivowel, who are the fifth musical note, who hold the Pināka! (13)
Homage to you who are the niṣāda note; homage to the lord of the Niṣādas;
Homage to you who take the form of instruments such as the lute, flute, and mṛdaṅga drum! (14)
Homage to the treble, to the bass, to the frightful one, to the one of benign form;
Homage to the one whose form is musical notes (tāna); homage to the master of melodic modulations (mūrcchanā)! (15)
Homage to the one whose form is aesthetic emotion, through the distinction of permanent and transitory states;
To the lover of musical rhythm, to rhythm itself, to the source of gentle and vigorous dances! (16)
To the one whose form is the triple arts of music, song, and dance; O great lover of the triple arts, / who through devotion rendered in the triple arts bestow the splendor of nirvāṇa! (17)
To the one whose form is gross and subtle, whose form is visible and invisible;

4.73.s: arvācīnāya ca namaḥ parācīnāya te namaḥ .. 18 ..
4.73.d: अर्वाचीनाय च नमः पराचीनाय ते नमः .. 18 ..
4.73.m: Homage to the near, and homage to you who are beyond! (18)

4.74.d: इत्थं क्षेत्रं सदा पांति गणा एतेऽति भास्वराः ..53..
4.74.m: In this manner, these extremely radiant gaṇas always guard the sacred field:
Kālākṣa, Raṇabhadra, Kauleya, and Kālakaṃpana—

4.74.s: ete pūrveṇa rakṣaṃti gaṃgāpāre sthitā gaṇāḥ .. 54 ..
4.74.d: एते पूर्वेण रक्षंति गंगापारे स्थिता गणाः .. 54 ..
4.74.m: stationed on the opposite bank of the Gaṅgā, these gaṇas protect in the east.
Vīrabhadra, Nabhas, Kardamāliptavigraha,
Sthūlakarṇa, and Mahābāhu are stationed across the Asi [river];
Viśālākṣa, Mahābhīma, Kuṇḍodara, and Mahodara,
stationed in the region of Dehalī, guard the western gate;
Nandisena, Pāñcāla, Kharapāda, Karaṇṭaka,
Ānando, Gopaka, and Babhru guard on the bank of the Varaṇā.
In that greatly meritorious sacred field is the liṅga named Oṃkāra.

4.74.s: tatra siddhiṃ parāṃ prāptā dehenānena sādhakāḥ .. 58 ..
4.74.d: तत्र सिद्धिं परां प्राप्ता देहेनानेन साधकाः .. 58 ..
4.74.m: There, practitioners achieved supreme perfection with this very body:
Kapila, Sāvarṇi, Śrīkaṇṭha, Piṅgala, and Aṃśumat—
these Pāśupatas were indeed perfected through the worship of that liṅga.
Once, having performed the worship of that liṅga, all five,
dancing with huḍuk-shouts, merged into that liṅga.
And another wonder that occurred there, I shall tell you;
listen, O wise one, O Damana, best of brahmins!

4.74.s: ekā bhekī mune tatra caraṃtī liṃga sannidhau ..
4.74.d: एका भेकी मुने तत्र चरंती लिंग सन्निधौ ..
4.74.m: A female frog, O sage, wandering there in the vicinity of the liṅga,
always made circumambulation, eating the unbroken grains of the floral offerings.

4.74.s: sā tatra mṛtyuṃ na prāpa śivanirmālyabhakṣaṇāt ..
4.74.d: सा तत्र मृत्युं न प्राप शिवनिर्माल्यभक्षणात् ..
4.74.m: She did not meet death there because of eating the offerings to Śiva;
her death occurred outside the sacred field because of that sin.
Better even to drink poison than to consume the property of Śiva;
poison kills a single person, [while] the property of Śiva destroys [one] down to sons and grandsons.
Those whose limbs are fattened on Śiva's property are not to be touched by good people.
By that ripening of karma, they then became dwellers in Raurava hell.
A certain crow, seeing that female frog hopping here and there,
took her in his beak and went outside the sacred field.

4.74.s: varṣābhvī tena sā kṣiptā kākena kṣetrabāhyataḥ ..
4.74.d: वर्षाभ्वी तेन सा क्षिप्ता काकेन क्षेत्रबाह्यतः ..
4.74.m: That frog was dropped outside the sacred field by that crow.

4.74.s: atha sā kālato bhekī tatraiva kṣetrasattame .. 67 ..
4.74.d: अथ सा कालतो भेकी तत्रैव क्षेत्रसत्तमे .. 67 ..
4.74.m: Then, in the course of time, that female frog, right there in that best of sacred fields,
from circumambulating and also touching the liṅga,
possessing both merit and demerit, was born as a girl in the house of Puṣpabaṭu.
She had an auspicious arrangement of limbs, endowed with auspicious marks;
however, she was born vulture-faced because of eating the unbroken grains of the floral offerings.
She knew thoroughly the secrets of singing and had an exceedingly sweet voice:
The seven musical notes, the three scales, the twenty-one melodic progressions,
the forty-nine melodic patterns, the one hundred and one rhythms,

4.74.s: rāgāḥ ṣaḍeva teṣāṃ tu paṃcapaṃcāpi cāṃganāḥ..71 ..
4.74.d: रागाः षडेव तेषां तु पंचपंचापि चांगनाः..71 ..
4.74.m: and the six rāgas, each having five female counterparts [rāgiṇīs]—
thirty-six rāgas and rāgiṇīs that bring joy to the impassioned;
and sixty-five other [sub-types] according to variations of place and time.

4.74.s: yāvaṃta eva tālāḥ syu rāgāstāvaṃta eva hi ..
4.74.d: यावंत एव तालाः स्यु रागास्तावंत एव हि ..
4.74.m: Indeed, as many rhythms as there are, just so many are the rāgas.
Thus, with this esoteric doctrine of song, daily that girl of auspicious vows,
Mādhavī, sweet of speech, would worship Omkāra.
Even having attained priceless youth, the daughter of Puṣpabaṭu,
by force of the latencies of her previous birth, thought highly indeed of Omkāra.
Her mind, naturally restless, attained steadfastness through control
by serving that liṅga, like [the mind] of a great soul through yoga.

4.74.s: na divā bādhayāṃcakre kṣuttṛṇnidrā kṣapā sutām .. 76 ..
4.74.d: न दिवा बाधयांचक्रे क्षुत्तृण्निद्रा क्षपा सुताम् .. 76 ..
4.74.m: Neither hunger, thirst, sleep, night, nor day tormented the girl;
she was untiring in mind in gazing upon that liṅga.
As many blinks of the eyes as she had by day and night,
so much time was considered a great obstacle by that virtuous girl.

4.74.s: nimeṣāṃtaritaḥ kālo yo yo vyathoṃgato mama ..
4.74.d: निमेषांतरितः कालो यो यो व्यथोंगतो मम ..
4.74.m: [She thought:] “Whatever time of mine has elapsed in the interval of a blink,
since I was not beholding the liṅga, what expiation could there be for that?”
Reflecting thus, she never abandoned the service of the syllable Om.
Desiring water, she would drink the nectar of the name of the liṅga.

4.74.s: nānya ddidṛkṣiṇī tasyā akṣiṇī śrutige api ..
4.74.d: नान्य द्दिदृक्षिणी तस्या अक्षिणी श्रुतिगे अपि ..
4.74.m: Her eyes, though reaching to her ears, desired to see nothing else,
leaving aside the Omkāra liṅga, which resides in the heart-sky of the virtuous.
Her two ears were intent on grasping no other sound;
her two hands became exceedingly skilled in making beautiful garlands for it.
Her two feet did not walk elsewhere in desire for pleasure,
having left the courtyard ground of Omkāra, trodden by the Lotus-born Lady of Liberation.
Omkāra, the Praṇava, the essence, the illuminator of the supreme Brahman,
whose form is the sound-Brahman and the three Vedas, the abode of nāda, bindu, and kalā,
the eternal imperishable syllable, the primal form, the cosmic form, the higher and the lower,
the boon, the worthy of choice, the giver of boons, eternal, tranquil, Īśvara,
the sole generator of all the worlds, the sole protector of all the worlds,
the sole destroyer of all the worlds, the solely praised of all the worlds,
without beginning or end, eternal, Śiva, Śaṃkara, imperishable,
the one beyond the three guṇas, who has made his abode in the hearts of his devotees,
devoid of limiting conditions, formless, changeless, unstained,
spotless, devoid of ego, beyond the phenomenal world, self-manifesting,
rejoicing in his own self, endless, all-pervading, all-seeing,
all-giving, all-enjoying, the all, the abode of all happiness—
her organ of speech, loudly pronouncing that [name] day and night,
did not utter any other name of anyone else at any time.
Tasting day and night the nectarous flavour of the syllables of this name,
her tongue knew no other taste whatsoever.
Sweeping and [drawing] festive patterns constantly around the temple,
Mādhavī would perform there, as well as the cleansing of the vessels for worship.

4.74.s: tatra pāśupatā ye vai praṇaveśārcane ratāḥ ..
4.74.d: तत्र पाशुपता ये वै प्रणवेशार्चने रताः ..
4.74.m: Those Pāśupatas who were devoted to the worship of the Lord of Praṇava there,
she would always serve with deep devotion, viewing them as her fathers.
Once, on the fourteenth day of the lunar month of Vaiśākha, that Mādhavī,
having kept a vigil at night and fasted during the day,
when the devotees gathered for the pilgrimage festival had departed in all directions in the morning,
performed sweeping and the rest, and joyfully worshipped the liṅga.
Singing a sweet song, dancing by her own natural grace,

4.74.s: dhyāyaṃtī liṃgamoṃkāraṃ tatra liṃge layaṃ yayau .. 95 ..
4.74.d: ध्यायंती लिंगमोंकारं तत्र लिंगे लयं ययौ .. 95 ..
4.74.m: meditating upon the liṅga as the Praṇava, she dissolved into that liṅga.
With this very earthly body, that highly intelligent maiden [dissolved],
as our chief teachers and ascetic sages watched.
The light that burst forth from the liṅga filled the sky like matted hair;

4.74.s: tatra jyotiṣi sā bālā jyotirmayyapi sāpyabhūt .. 97 ..
4.74.d: तत्र ज्योतिषि सा बाला ज्योतिर्मय्यपि साप्यभूत् .. 97 ..
4.74.m: into that light the girl, also transformed into light, entered.
Even today, on the fourteenth day of the bright half of Vaiśākha, the residents of the sacred field
undertake a pilgrimage there, accompanied by a great festival.
Having kept a night-vigil there and fasted on the fourteenth day,

4.74.s: prāpnuvaṃti paraṃ jñānaṃ yatrakutrāpi vai mṛtāḥ .. 99 ..
4.74.d: प्राप्नुवंति परं ज्ञानं यत्रकुत्रापि वै मृताः .. 99 ..
4.74.m: they attain supreme knowledge, wherever they may die.

4.74.s: brahmāṃḍodara madhye tu yāni tīrthāni sarvataḥ ..
4.74.d: ब्रह्मांडोदर मध्ये तु यानि तीर्थानि सर्वतः ..
4.74.m: Whatever sacred fords there are everywhere inside the cosmic egg,
they all come to behold Oṃkāra on the fourteenth day of Vaiśākha.
In front of the liṅga is a most excellent cave named Śrīmukhī;

4.74.s: pātālasya ca taddvāraṃ tatra siddhā vasaṃti hi .. 1 ..
4.74.d: पातालस्य च तद्द्वारं तत्र सिद्धा वसंति हि .. 1 ..
4.74.m: it is the entrance to Pātāla, and indeed perfected beings dwell there.

4.74.s: tiṣṭheyuḥ paṃcarātraṃ ye guhāyāṃ tatra suvratāḥ ..
4.74.d: तिष्ठेयुः पंचरात्रं ये गुहायां तत्र सुव्रताः ..
4.74.m: Those observing good vows who stay for five nights in that cave
behold serpent maidens, and they speak of what is auspicious and inauspicious.
In the northern direction of the cave there is a well whose water is an elixir;
drinking of it for six months, one drinks the elixir of Brahman.
Having seen the liṅga Nādeśvara there, one becomes the source of cosmic sound;
the universe, consisting entirely of sound, becomes an object within range of his ears.
Bathing there in the Matsyodarī, the celestial river filled by the Varuṇā,
a creature fulfills all obligations and never grieves anywhere.
Countless devotees of Oṃkāreśvara have attained perfection
with their earthly bodies, which instantly became divine.
Avimukta is the supreme sacred field, beyond even the entire cosmic egg;

4.74.s: tatopi para oṃkāra ukto matsyodarī taṭe .. 7 ..
4.74.d: ततोपि पर ओंकार उक्तो मत्स्योदरी तटे .. 7 ..
4.74.m: even beyond that is declared Oṃkāra on the bank of the Matsyodarī.

4.74.s: praṇaveśoṃ'ga yaiḥ kāśyāṃ na nato nāpi cārcitaḥ ..
4.74.d: प्रणवेशोंऽग यैः काश्यां न नतो नापि चार्चितः ..
4.74.m: O dear one, by whom Praṇaveśa has neither been bowed to nor worshipped in Kāśī—
for what purpose were they born, robbers of their mother's youth?
Ever since the Lord of the Universe came from Mount Mandara
into that forest of bliss, ever since then, O best of men,
all sanctuaries quickly went [there] from that time on,

4.74.s: sa nadīni sa tīrthāni sa dvīpāni yayustataḥ .. .. 4.2.74.110 ..
4.74.m: along with the oceans, the mountains, the rivers, the sacred fords, and the continents.

4.74.s: idānīṃ mama bhāgyena smāritohaṃ tvayā mune ..
4.74.d: इदानीं मम भाग्येन स्मारितोहं त्वया मुने ..
4.74.m: Now, by my good fortune, I have been reminded by you, O sage;
I too shall come; let us go slowly to Kāśī.
These disciples of mine as well, who maintain the great Pāśupata vow,
they too wish to go to Kāśī, since all desire liberation.

4.74.s: api vārdhakamāsādya yaiḥ kāśī naiva śīlitā ..
4.74.d: अपि वार्धकमासाद्य यैः काशी नैव शीलिता ..
4.74.m: Even upon reaching old age, those by whom Kāśī has not been frequented—
when rare human birth is lost, whence will supreme happiness come to them?
As long as there is no impairment of the senses, as long as there is no decay of lifespan,
so long should Śambhu's forest of bliss be resorted to with effort.
Those who have taken refuge in Śambhu's forest of bliss, the abode of fortune—
unwavering fortune shall not abandon them, the unique treasuries of great joy.
Having related this delightful story, Garga, the best of Pāśupatas,
along with Bhāradvāja, reached the city of Vārāṇasī.
Even Damana, righteous of soul, accompanied by the teacher Garga,
worshipped glorious Oṃkāra and dissolved into that liṅga.
Skanda said:
O enemy of Ilvala, the supreme abode Oṃkāra is in Avimukta;

4.74.s: tatra siddhiparāṃ jagmuḥ sādhakā bahuśo mune .. 18 ..
4.74.d: तत्र सिद्धिपरां जग्मुः साधका बहुशो मुने .. 18 ..
4.74.m: there, practitioners have attained supreme perfection in great numbers, O sage.
In the Kali age, it must never be spoken before those of defiled minds,
especially the māhātmya of Praṇaveśvara before unbelievers.

4.74.s: ye niṃdaṃti mahādevaṃ kṣetraṃ niṃdaṃti ye'dhiyaḥ ..
4.74.d: ये निंदंति महादेवं क्षेत्रं निंदंति येऽधियः ..
4.74.m: Those who revile Mahādeva, the fools who revile the sacred field,

4.74.s: purāṇaṃ ye ca niṃdaṃti te saṃbhāṣyā na kutracit .. 4.2.74.120 ..
4.74.m: and those who revile the Purāṇa—one should never converse with them anywhere.
There is no liṅga equal to Oṃkāra anywhere on the surface of the earth;
this was definitively declared to Gaurī by the God of gods.
Having heard this chapter, a person with mind fixed upon it,
freed from all sins, shall attain the world of Śiva.

4.74.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ caturthekāśīkhaṃḍa uttarārdha oṃkāramāhātmyaṃ nāma catuḥsaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 74 ..
4.74.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां चतुर्थेकाशीखंड उत्तरार्ध ओंकारमाहात्म्यं नाम चतुःसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः .. 74 ..
4.74.m: Thus ends the seventy-fourth chapter, titled 'The Māhātmya of Oṃkāra,' in the second half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa, in the fourth [part] of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

4.75.m:
Agastya said:
Having heard this story of Oṃkāra, which destroys great sins, / I am not yet satiated, O Viśākha; now tell the story of the celestial [liṅga]. 1
And how was it spoken to the Goddess by the God of gods, O six-faced one? / [Tell of] the highest, sacred manifestation of Trilocana, O of great intellect! 2
Skanda said:
Listen, O sage, I shall tell the story that dispels fatigue, / just as it was related by the God, concerning the origin of Triviṣṭapa. 3
For that seat is called Virajā, and there is the Triviṣṭapa liṅga; / merely by the darśana of that seat, a man becomes free from passion. 4
Indeed, three flowing streams are joined there, O pot-born [sage]— / three destroyers of blemishes, to the south of Trilocana. 5
Assuming the forms of streams in visible form for the sake of bathing the liṅga, / the Sarasvatī, then the Kālindī, and the Narmadā, bestowing immense bliss, 6
all three of these rivers, with pitchers in hand at the three junctures of the day, / bathe the great abode, the mighty celestial liṅga. 7
Liṅgas were also established by them all around, bearing their own names; / by the darśana of these, men obtain the fruit of a bath in them. 8
The Sarasvatīśvara liṅga, to the south of Triviṣṭapa, / grants the realm of Sarasvatī when seen and touched, and removes dullness. 9
And the Yamuneśa in the west, worshipped with devotion by men, / even by those who possess sin, averts the realm of Yama. 10
Seen to the east of Trilocana, Narmadeśa bestows great bliss; / by worshipping that liṅga, entry into a womb is prevented for men. 11
Having bathed in the Pilipilā tīrtha near Triviṣṭapa / and having seen the Trilocana liṅga, why would one grieve any further? 12
Even by the mere remembrance of the Triviṣṭapa liṅga, a mortal / will become the lord of heaven; no doubt should be entertained here. 13
Those who behold Triviṣṭapa become creators, without doubt; / they alone are fulfilled in their purpose here, they alone are truly wise here. 14
Those by whom the Triviṣṭapa liṅga was bowed to in Ānandakānana, / and by whom, with purified intellect, even the name of Trilocana was heard, 15
are purified from sin acquired in seven births; of this there is no doubt. / Whatever fruit is obtained from seeing all the liṅgas upon earth, 16
that would be obtained upon seeing Triviṣṭapa, and I deem it even greater in Kāśī; / when Triviṣṭapa is seen in Kāśī, all heaven is seen. 17
In a moment his sin is shaken off, and he will not partake of a womb again; / he has bathed in all tīrthas, and he has performed the concluding ablutions of all sacrifices— 18
he who indeed bathes in the north-flowing waters at the Pilipilā tīrtha, / where the greatly holy triad of rivers dwells visibly forever. 19
Having performed the śrāddha and other rites there, what will he do at Gayā? / Having bathed at the Pilipilā tīrtha and made the offering of the piṇḍa, 20
and having seen the Triviṣṭapa liṅga, one obtains the fruit of ten million tīrthas. / Whatever sin is acquired elsewhere departs upon seeing Kāśī; 21
but whatever sin is committed in Kāśī bestows the state of a piśāca. / If one has committed a sin out of negligence in Śambhu's Ānandakānana, 22
even that sin one will abandon upon seeing the Triviṣṭapa liṅga. / In all the earth's surface, Ānandakānana is supreme; 23
even there, all the tīrthas [are present], and superior even to that is the realm of Oṃkāra; / and even greater than the true liṅga of Oṃkāra that illumines the path to liberation, 24
most supreme is the liṅga of Trilocana, the very embodiment of the highest good. 25
Just as the sun is among luminous bodies, and as the moon among things to be seen, / so among all liṅgas the supreme liṅga is Trilocana. 26
For the worshippers of Trilocana, that status is not far off— / the supreme treasure of great happiness belonging to the lotus-like nirvāṇa. 27
The ultimate good which is acquired from worshipping Trilocana once / cannot be obtained by worshipping other liṅgas accumulated over a lifetime. 28
Those of great intellect who worship the Trilocana liṅga in Kāśī / are worthy of worship by the dwellers of the three worlds who desire my favour. 29
Even having renounced everything, having undertaken the Pāśupata vow, / and even having fallen from the observances, why do mortals fear, 30
when there exists this great liṅga that carries away the flood of great sins— / Triviṣṭapa, an accumulation of merit, the abode depositing liberation? 31
Having fully worshipped the great liṅga, Trilocana, only once, / one is freed from all defilements, even those accumulated over a hundred births. 32
Even a slayer of a brahmin, or a drinker of liquor, a thief, or one who violates the teacher’s bed, / or one who associates with such a person for a year, who is proclaimed a great sinner, 33
or one devoted to another’s wife, or one devoted to violence against others, / or one whose habit is slander of others, as well as a betrayer of trust, 34

even one ungrateful, an aborticide, or the husband of a śūdra woman,
one who abandons mother, father, or teacher, an incendiary, or a poisoner,
a slayer of a cow, a slayer of a woman, a slayer of a śūdra, or a defiler of a maiden,
or one who is cruel, or a tale-bearer, or one who has turned away from his own duty,

or an eater of forbidden food, and likewise a seller of what should not be sold—

attains expiation from sin upon bowing to the Trilocana liṅga. 38
The fool devoted to reviling Śiva, who censures the scriptures of Śiva—
no expiation for him is seen anywhere, even in scripture, by anyone. 39
He should be known as a slayer of his own self, always a slayer of the three worlds;
he who undertakes the reviling of Śiva is the lowest of the low, not to be spoken to. 40
And those who are devoted to reviling Śiva, or even against the devotees of Śiva,
go to a dreadful hell for as long as the moon and the sun endure. 41
Śaivas must be worshipped diligently in Kāśī by those desiring liberation;
even when they are worshipped, Śiva becomes pleased without doubt. 42

With the desire to make expiation for all sins here,
this word ought to be spoken without hesitation by those who know authoritative means of knowledge: 43
“If you desire the preliminary rite, if you are afraid of sin,
if you consider our word true on the authority of scriptures,
then, having renounced everything, having made a firm resolve in your mind,
Go to the Ānandakānana, where Viśveśvara himself dwells,
where, for men who enter the sacred field with resolute minds,
the accumulation of sin does not afflict them, and the highest righteousness is attained.
Even today there is a great sacred ford there, exceedingly pure with three streams,
holy, named Pilipilā, served by three rivers,
by a glance from Trilocana's eye dispelling great sin.

with incense, lamps, food offerings, garments, and many ornaments,

with recitations, circumambulations, and joyous prostrations,
and having thus performed complete worship by satisfying the attendants,
one should then have the brahmins declare, saying: 'I am free from sin.'
A wise man doing thus becomes free from sin in an instant.
Then having bathed at Pañcanada, and then in the Maṇikarṇī pool,
and then worshipping the Lord of the Universe (Viśveśa), one attains great merit.
This expiation has been declared as that which purifies from great sins;
it must not be spoken to an unbeliever, nor to one who reviles the Kāśīmāhātmya.
And if one gives this auspicious expiation out of greed for wealth,
the giver goes to hell; this is true, truly true, O pot-born [Agastya]!
The fruit that is fully attained by circumambulating the earth
is obtained at twilight in Kāśī by circumambulating Trilocana seven times.

4.75.m:
Having seen in Kāśī the Triviṣṭapa liṅga whose girdle is a serpent,
one would become liberated in another birth even if death takes place elsewhere.
Elsewhere, among all liṅgas, an auspicious time is distinguished;
at Triviṣṭapa, the auspicious time for men is always, day and night.
The liṅgas beginning with Oṃkāra are fully capable of cutting off all sins,
yet the power of Trilocana is something entirely different, O Pārvatī.
The reason why among all liṅgas this liṅga is supreme,
listen to that reason, O Aparṇā; lend an ear, and I shall tell you.
Formerly, while I was united in yoga, this great liṅga
split open the seven subterranean realms (Pātāla) and emerged from the surface of the earth before me.
When I remained deeply hidden in this liṅga long ago, O Gaurī,
the three eyes were granted to you, and so you beheld the Supreme.
From that time forward, O goddess of the gods, this Trilocana liṅga
is praised by the dwellers of the three worlds as bestowing the vision of knowledge.
Those who are devotees of Trilocana are themselves also three-eyed;

No one knows fully the greatness of the Trilocana liṅga,
O Great Goddess, for it has been concealed by me alone.
Having bathed in the Pailipila pool on the third day of the bright half of Vaiśākha,
devoted to fasting with devotion, keeping vigil at night,
having worshipped Trilocana and also bathed there in the morning,
worshipping the liṅga again, and giving pots of righteousness (dharmaghaṭa)
filled with food and sacrificial fees, O goddess, gladly offered for the sake of the ancestors,
and then breaking the fast together with devotees of Śiva,
shedding the earthly body, impelled by that merit,
they certainly become gaṇas leading in my presence, O goddess.
Gods, mortals, and great serpents wander in worldly existence only so long,
O Gaurī, as they do not behold the Trilocana liṅga in Kāśī.
Having seen Triviṣṭapa once and bathed in the Pailipila pool,
a creature is never again born here to suck a mother's breast.

4.75.m:
Every month, on the eighth and fourteenth days, O beautiful one,
all the sacred fords come to behold the god Triviṣṭapa.
One who has bathed in the Pailipila waters to the south of Triviṣṭapa,
and worshipped the twilight there once, obtains the fruit of a Rājasūya sacrifice.
Right there is the well named Pādodaka, which destroys all sins.
Having drunk its water, a mortal is not born as a mortal again. // 75
Beside that liṅga, indeed, there are numerous liṅgas;
they bestow liberation here simply by darśana and by touch. // 76
There is the Śāṃtanava liṅga established on the bank of the Gaṅgā;
having seen it, a man tormented by worldly existence attains peace. // 77
To its south, O sage, is the great liṅga called Bhīṣmeśa;
from the sight of it, Kali, Death, and desire do not torment [one]. // 78
To the west of it is the great liṅga proclaimed as Droṇeśa,
by worshipping which liṅga Droṇa assumed a form of light once again. // 79
In front of it is the Aśvatthāmeśvara liṅga, bestowing immense merit,

This advice should be given by men to one who desires to go to Kedāra:
“Touching Kedāra in Kāśī, you will have accomplished your purpose.”
Having observed a fast on the fourteenth day of the dark half of Caitra,

He who bows to the Lord of Kedāra three times a day for up to six months,
to him the world protectors, Yama and the others, continually bow.

Having seen the Lord of Kedāra once, O goddess, one becomes my attendant.
Therefore, with great effort, one should behold the Lord of Kedāra in Kāśī.
North of Kedāra is the auspicious liṅga Citrāṅgadeśvara;
from worshipping it, a man continually enjoys the delights of heaven.
